I started thinking about this earlier today and wondered if anyone has some info they could provide on the topic; opinion or factual. How economic is gaming? In the 'thrifty management' sense. How sustainable is it? Are there companies that care about these things?

You have a game company, a group of friends make a game and decide to publish it. They need a manufacturer/printer, more than likely they'll go over seas. Have they visited that place? Where are the manufacturer's sourcing their materials from? What are the working conditions like? A LOT of paper products go into gaming and in my favorite type of game (miniature gaming), a lot of plastics- oil; what are the source companies doing to be sustainable?

If you've published games, I'd absolutely love your insight to these types of questions.

If you're a lover of games, like me, I'd be so happy to get your opinion on the topic.

Thanks!

Also, I know the topic of cost comes up a lot in these kinds of conversations and, I'd like to move beyond that. For the most part, yes, it'd be more expensive to manufacture locally and with more sustainable practices but, let's try to move beyond a conversation about money.

Can we handle repost? Sometimes repost is needed (intentional) and sometimes it is by accident and sometimes there is evil intention also.

mechanism

Currently any post has 3 interactive parts: 1. Clickable title (link), 2. discuss/view comment, 3. save. Add two more button to the post: "repost" and "original discuss". Then the post itself has flag, either original or reposted.

The "repost" button is available for post with original status. When clicked, it prompt the title and subverse where it want to be reposted. Any post submitted using the "repost" button is flagged as "reposted".

The "original discuss" button is available for post with "reposted" status. When clicked, it goes to discussion of original post.

When the reposted post get upvoted, the original also get upvote. The same with downvote, except that the downvote to original is capped at 0.

Mod flag

Now rather than deleting repost, mod can flag the post as "reposted". The effect is same as described above.

Report repost

Hopefully user can help to report repost to mod. This will help mod to take action to reposted post faster.

I remember seeing someone bring this up in /v/videos and it prevented them from posting the video link they were about to submit. That's cool and all but maybe there should be a timer to allow for reposts. Like a month or so, just to let it sink in since there are some subs where old content would be welcome if it is buried under tons of other content.

I have thought about that. No, my idea here does not prevent any reposted post to be posted. It does not handle submission. It provide another way to submit: submission by reposting. The original submission is stay the same. The submission by reposting works as described above.

Another mechanism I introduced is flagging post as reposted. Post that has already submitted, after identified, can be marked as reposted by mod. The reposted submission will provide link to original submission. No deletion or prevention at all.
Cool. I like the idea to link to the original post. I hope to see it implemented in some way!

I was super obnoxious. There was this one older guy though. Probably in his mid 30's, he was super cool, and totally understood me. Was probably the closest thing I had to a best friend at the time. Always made the work nights better. He'd help me close up by moping the floors and screaming, "I'm sorry mama! I didn't mean to make you cry, but tonight, I'm moppin up the floors!" The owner (his brother-in-law) would often come back and tell us to keep it down because they'd still have the bar open. Really great memories from a not so great time in my life.

Seether: First boyfriend when I was 16. He was amazing. Didn't work out, obviously, but again, great memories.

My dog had been hit by a car the night before and I had been the one to scrape what was left of her off the pavement and into a garbage bag in the dark. Somehow I was sorta numb about it though and ended up going to sleep, waking and leaving for work the next morning all in darkness. I got caught up in work and kinda forgot the whole thing until my drive home, which was in bright daylight.

Ferry Corsten's Shelter Me was the song playing on my mp3 player as I drove up on the skid marks on the road which showed where she had been hit and where she had been dragged to. I must have missed a bit of her in the dark at night because that little bit had been smeared down the road due to passing traffic. The bittersweet breakdown at 2:20 of this song will forever remind me of that moment and the realization of what she went through in her last moments. I barely managed to pull into my driveway before bursting into tears remembering that she wouldn't be at the door to greet me.

Maverick, you were a badass dog and I'll never forget you.
